solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: My unit — revolting!

indicators.note: the letters of the two words rise up against their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer exclaims in dismay that their own unit has risen up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' rearranges MYUNIT, and the whole clue also describes the answer: a unit in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebellion by soldiers or sailors against their officers is exactly a unit revolting.

clue.text: Parent brought over difficult dog

indicators.note: in a down answer the word for parent is turned round before going in

parts.note: am is the reverse of ma, a mother
stiff, as in a stiff test, means difficult

explanation.surface: A mother has carried round a hard-to-handle dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' turns AM into MA; 'difficult' gives STIFF as in a stiff exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, powerful breed kept as a guard animal is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Narrator welcoming artist, Victor, one on the move

indicators.note: the storyteller takes in the following pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a teller is one who tells a story
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
V is Victor in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A storyteller receives a painter and a man called Victor, someone always travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock artist; 'welcoming' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who journeys from place to place is always on the move.

clue.text: Cloud, new, blue for a change, over America

indicators.note: the word blue is altered into a new order of its letters

explanation.surface: A fresh cloud, blue for once, drifts above America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is only a link: in a down entry the first pieces sit above America.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy a vast interstellar mass of gas and dust is a cloud.

clue.text: Boy songs excite one definitely from the start, lively

indicators.note: the gathered letters are set jumping about into a new order
the opening letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: A lad's songs thrill one, certainly from the beginning, with spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the start' takes E, O, D; 'lively' shuffles them with SONGS. 'Boy' looks like a lad, but is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as exclamations of surprise: 'Oh boy!' and 'My word!' say the same thing.

clue.text: So uncommon, exceptional, kinky — in the end unique

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: Something so rare, outstanding and quirky is ultimately one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' takes O, N, L, Y from the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one of a kind is the sole example, single and alone.

clue.text: View yard — potentially somewhere to park

indicators.note: the letters could become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Look over a yard that could serve for parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges VIEWYARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A private road up to a house is where a car is commonly left.

clue.text: Avoid poster, boring the day before

indicators.note: the advert drills into the middle of the other word

parts.note: eve is the evening or day before an event
an ad, advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: Steer clear of the dull poster from the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull, but here it means drilling into: the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape or dodge something is to avoid it.

clue.text: At sea respect symbol of power

indicators.note: being all at sea is confusion, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Sailors far from land honour the emblem of authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges RESPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ceremonial staff is an emblem of royal authority.

clue.text: Quiet religious building English must leave, past its best

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: the letter for English departs from the building's name

parts.note: an abbey is a monastic church

explanation.surface: A quiet church that the English have to abandon is now run down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must leave' takes E out of ABBEY to give ABBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn and threadbare things are tatty, no longer in good condition.

clue.text: Edging away, cult writer's visiting gallery last

indicators.note: the outer letters, the edges, are dropped from the word cult
the writer's piece goes in to call on the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery
the writer is 'I', so writer's is I'm, I am

explanation.surface: Losing its fringe, a cult author is at the gallery at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery; the writer is 'I', so writer's means 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Final and eventual both mean coming at the end, the last in a series.

clue.text: One glib, wretched, base

indicators.note: something wretched is in a sorry state, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking person, miserable and lowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wretched' rearranges ONEGLIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of mean and dishonourable, lacking any nobility.

clue.text: Beliefs unusually good, i.e. extremely lofty

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unusual order, so they are rearranged
the outer letters, at the extremes of the word, are taken

explanation.surface: Principles that are remarkably good, that is, very high-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives LY from lofty; 'unusually' shuffles GOOD, IE and LY together.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of ideas and doctrines held by a group is a body of convictions.

clue.text: One in charge for limited period maybe, initially rather exacting guy

definitions.text: One in charge for limited period maybe

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: a gent, gentleman, is a guy

explanation.surface: A temporary boss perhaps, at first a rather demanding fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R and E; a GENT is a guy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rules on behalf of an underage or absent monarch governs for a time only.

clue.text: Having succeeded aboard, abandon course

indicators.note: the letter goes on board, inside the other word

parts.note: to desert is to abandon
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Having made it on to a ship, someone forsakes their path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' puts S inside DESERT. 'course' looks like a route, but it is part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet part of a meal served after the main dish is one course.

clue.text: Where there's nothing odd, if you like people

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are thrown out, so only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: A place free of strangeness, if you like those around you.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of IFYOULIKE leaves F, O, L, K.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary men and women together are folks or persons in general.

clue.text: E.g. field of rice to start with, no longer abundant

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the three words is taken

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in that role
ample means plentiful

explanation.surface: Take a paddy, which once was plentiful, as an instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start with' takes F, O, R from field, of, rice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation e.g., exempli gratia, is read as 'for instance'.

clue.text: Goody-goody crossing nasty one finally? Right

indicators.note: the word for nasty crosses into the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteous, goody-goody person
vile means nasty

indicators.note: the last letter of the word one is taken

explanation.surface: A smug type passing a horrid person at last? Fair enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like agreement after the question, but it is the noun: an entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A right in the sense of a special entitlement or advantage granted to someone.

clue.text: Note the French drop programme

parts.note: te is a note in sol-fa
le is French for the
to cast is to throw or shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: Note how the French let a show fall.
explanation.walkthrough: TE is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale; CAST means shed, as in casting off.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast on television is a show or programme.

clue.text: Early 20th century movement dashed rulers' aims

indicators.note: the hopes are dashed, smashed up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The monarchs' ambitions were thwarted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed' rearranges RULERSAIMS (the apostrophe adds no letter).
explanation.definitionFit: The art movement of Dalí and Magritte began in the 1920s.

clue.text: Coming up, argues at intervals over difficult situation — better

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters rise, so they are read from bottom to top
every other letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a pass, as in 'things came to a pretty pass', is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: Approaching, someone quarrels now and then about a tight spot, to outdo it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes RUS from argues; 'Coming up' turns it into SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to do better than, exceed or outdo; 'better' is used here as a verb.

clue.text: Prejudice from article included in another time

indicators.note: the article is put inside the other word

parts.note: bis means again, a second time, as a call for an encore
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Prejudice from a newspaper piece reappears at a later date.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS, Latin for twice, is the call for an encore or a direction to repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice and partiality are a leaning or slant one way.

clue.text: Level of skills upset corporation

indicators.note: in a down answer the word is set upside down, read backwards

parts.note: arts are skills or crafts
corporation is a dated joke word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A tier of talents turned over a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ARTS into STRA; corporation means a paunch, so TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of rock or of society is one level or stratum.

clue.text: Bright hearts maybe — extremely natural to be captivated

indicators.note: the outer pick is held captive inside the other word

parts.note: hearts is one example of a suit of cards

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word natural are taken

explanation.surface: Lovers, cheerful perhaps, are naturally charmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts maybe' points to the card suit, of which hearts is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A place lit by the sun is bright.

clue.text: Not so careful — streaky stuff?

explanation.surface: Someone less cautious leaves a streaky mess.
explanation.definitionFit: More reckless or hasty is the comparative of reckless; streaky bacon is sliced into thin strips.

clue.text: Irrational to be taken in by vendor not half delivering this

definitions.text: Irrational to be taken in by vendor not half delivering this

indicators.note: the number goes inside the shortened word for vendor
half the letters of the vendor's word are dropped

parts.note: a seller is a vendor
pi is an irrational number

explanation.surface: A salesman delivers patter that is not wholly rational.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi is the classic irrational number. The whole clue also describes a salesman's patter, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib persuasive talk is the patter a salesperson delivers.

clue.text: Person who gave news about Open University policy at start one's seen at table

indicators.note: the town crier goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a town crier announced news in the streets

indicators.note: the opening letter of policy is taken

explanation.surface: A town crier talks of an Open University policy at the start of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university; a town crier called out news in the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino employee who runs a gaming table and deals cards is seen there.

clue.text: Flower briefly pleased

explanation.surface: A short-lived bloom brings delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for gladiolus, a garden bloom; and happy, delighted.

clue.text: A piece of sound equipment up to it, without dispute

parts.note: a mic, microphone, picks up sound
able means capable, up to the job

explanation.surface: A microphone that's fit for purpose, no arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and peaceable, settled with no quarrel or fighting.

clue.text: Legal claim in court — one seeking solicitor's advice?

indicators.note: the legal claim sits inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: a lien is a right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A lien in court involves someone after legal advice.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIEN is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who engages a lawyer is that lawyer's customer.

clue.text: Anxiety, having lost heart, being alone

indicators.note: the central letters are removed from the word for anxiety

parts.note: solicitude means anxious concern

explanation.surface: Worry, after losing courage, at being on one's own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' removes the middle CI from SOLICITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being by oneself, in seclusion, is a state of isolation.

clue.text: Current broadcast

explanation.surface: A flow that is transmitted.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook or flow of water is a current; to stream is to broadcast live online.
